source.title: What Do Sparse Autoencoder Feature Discovery Scores Identify? From Activations to Interventions
source.authors: Yi-Feng Guo; Yan-Ran Li; Xiang Chen

page_placements.theme: Detection, decodability and recurrence do not establish selective control

record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE latents as feature-discovery and intervention targets, but its experiments concern whether observational scores predict intervention effects, not whether superposition occurs or what its geometry is.
record.gate_note: The reported results compare SAE feature scores and probe-based predictions with intervention attributions and realized ablations. They do not measure feature overlap, near-orthogonality, polysemanticity, capacity pressure, SAE recovery as evidence of superposition, canonicality, or feature dimensionality. The adjacent intervention-prediction findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study uses public SAEs and their latents as intervention targets and compares observational scores (FDFI, probes, correlations) with gradient-based attribution and realized steering/ablation effects. It does not measure superposition, polysemanticity, capacity allocation, SAE recovery of features as evidence of superposition, feature canonicality or dimensionality. The second-dictionary check (Table E.3) compares the probe gap across SAEs, not feature stability.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors show that observational feature-discovery statistics do not in general identify intervention attribution, and derive an exact three-term decomposition of the probe–attribution gap. They find the gap large across four model-SAE pairs and propose attribution as the target for predicting and selecting SAE latents for intervention.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates observational SAE feature scores versus intervention attribution; it does not reproduce the toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Prediction gaps and intervention accuracy vary with the probe summary, intervention type, steering displacement, and feature-selection rule. The study also reports that first-order predictions break down more often at larger steering scales.

fits_no_version.finding: For single-latent zero-ablations, prompt-specific gradient predictions match the realized sign in 91–97% of rows with nonzero effects, versus 17–35% for final-position probe predictions, across four model-SAE pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-based intervention attribution predicts realized SAE-latent ablation effects better than observational linear-probe predictions.

fits_no_version.finding: Under unit steering, the median attribution of FDFI-selected latents is 2.8–4.6% of the probe coefficient. Coefficient-selected latents overstate small-step steering by about two orders of magnitude (Tables E.1, E.2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Observational association scores for SAE latents greatly overstate their first-order intervention effects.

record.problems: The experiments cover four model-SAE pairs at one layer each and use teacher-forced outputs. Llama-3.1-8B has few selected pairs in several analyses. Some steering comparisons and selection-rule analyses are descriptive or post hoc. The authors report simulated undercoverage of Stein-residual intervals under their sparse JumpReLU design (0.820 to 0.835 at observed stratum sizes).
record.rows_left_out: Other reported intervention-prediction, ranking, and held-out set-ablation results were not included because they concern the same adjacent construct and do not test any listed claim version.

untested.parts: Toy-model superposition, sparsity-dependent phase transition, near-orthogonal geometry: not studied.
Capacity-driven polysemanticity and allocation of dimensions by importance: not studied.
Polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure: not studied.
Whether LLM features spread across neurons or are recoverable by SAEs: SAEs are used, not evaluated for recovery.
Completeness, stability and canonicality of SAE features: not measured. The alternate-dictionary check concerns the probe–attribution gap only.
One-dimensional versus multi-dimensional features: not studied.

record.verdict_notes: The study bears on SAE use for steering and ablation, not on superposition itself. No version verdicts are given. All four rows compare the study's own method against a baseline and are linked to no version.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or allocates dedicated dimensions to more important features.
Whether polysemanticity can arise without capacity pressure, and whether it indicates superposition.
Whether LLM features spread across neurons or are sparse features recoverable by SAEs.
Completeness, stability, and canonicality of SAE features as units of model representation.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.
